# `Scanner/NoWrap-v1` · The fastest geometry without wrap-around

**B · Spatial encoding and reconstruction** · Fourier encoding · kind 2, set · isolates B9: Field of view: the sampling step of k-space; a larger object folds over. [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** ADMITTED: on 300 fresh instances per level the reference passes >= 99 %, no policy that ignores the object passes more than 6 % (95 % bounds)

The first decision of an examination. A hidden test object lies in the 1.5 T scanner. The agent looks (a localiser costs scan time), then prescribes the geometry of a spin-echo scan whose time grows with the number of phase-encode lines. The field of view can be moved and turned, so the fastest geometry depends on where the object lies, how large it is and which way it points.

Kind of task: **measurement** (one fixed localiser and a fixed estimator (`open_loop`) is the reference policy itself: no scan depends on an earlier one).

```python
import mrgym
env = mrgym.make("Scanner/NoWrap-v1", level=2, seed=0)
obs, info = env.reset()
obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step({"name": "scanner_info", "arguments": {}})
```

| Given | Deliver | Scored by |
|---|---|---|
| An object of hidden size, position and orientation; the scanner; 30 s of scan time for localisers | Geometry of a spin-echo scan: phase-encode axis, field of view, phase field of view, matrix, centre, rotation | Re-scan on the hidden object: whole object inside, no wrap-around, pixel as required, scan time within 10 % of the fastest such geometry |

## World

- On the table: QA phantom (an elliptical disc of gel with vials), 1.5 T
- Sequences that matter here: spgr, se
- Formulas the agent is given: scan time = overhead + dummy cycle + TR x phase-encode lines; the readout is oversampled and does not wrap; the phase-encode direction wraps unless the encoded field of view covers the object; pixel i of n is centred at centre + (i - n / 2) x pixel

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| size, position and orientation of the object | the target sequence and the required pixel size |
| its materials | the pass rule and its time factor |
| fields and system state | the instrument datasheet |
| noise level | realised protocol, timing, limits and cost of every plan and scan |
| the 128-bit world seed | any stored image, and the numbers along any line through it (the extent of the object has to be read from them) |

## Levels

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'pe_dir': 'y | x', 'fov_mm': '<mm>', 'phase_fov': '<fraction>', 'matrix': '<even integer>', 'centre_y_mm': '<mm>', 'centre_x_mm': '<mm>', 'rotation_deg': '<degrees>', 'phase_oversampling': '<fraction, optional>'}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan; the console accepts the geometry; pixel <= the required size; the whole object lies inside the image (hidden outline, 0.5 mm slack); wrap-around energy of a noise-free re-scan <= 0.002 of the image; scan time <= 1.1 x the scan time of the fastest geometry that passes the gates above (exhaustive search on the hidden world)
- Error: `T / T_opt - 1: scan time of the delivered geometry over the oracle's optimum`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates

## Gate: the control policies on fresh instances

Run 2026-11-25 on engine `mrgym-engine-0.2.0`, package 0.1.0.dev0: `mrgym gate Scanner/NoWrap-v1 --n 300 --write` (split gate, seeds 0..299; recipes tuned on split tune, seeds <set 0..2>:<0..15>). A level is admitted when the lower bound of the reference is at least 90 %, the upper bound of every must-fail policy is at most 10 % and every ablation required at the level loses at least 25 points (lower bound of the paired difference). Bounds are one-sided, 95 %. Cells: passed / instances (rate; bound).

| Policy | Must | Level 2 | Level 3 | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reference` | pass | 300/300 (100.0 %; lower bound 99.0 %) | 300/300 (100.0 %; lower bound 99.0 %) | one localiser; phase-encode axis along the narrowest direction of the bright pixels, field of view centred on them |
| `prior` | fail | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | no scan; the geometry that is safe for any object |
| `console_default` | fail | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | one token scan, then the console's default field of view, centred, phase along y |
| `fixed_recipe` | fail | 12/300 (4.0 %; upper bound 6.4 %) | 4/300 (1.3 %; upper bound 3.0 %) | one token scan, then one constant geometry (axis, rotation, lines; centred) tuned on other worlds |
| `brute_force` | fail | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | shrinks a centred square field of view scan by scan until the object touches its border |
| `wrong_units` | fail | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | the reference's geometry with every length in centimetres |
| `size_only` | ablation | 4/300 (1.3 %; 98.7 points below the reference, lower bound 97.6) | 3/300 (1.0 %; 99.0 points below the reference, lower bound 98.0) | the right size and direction, with the field of view left on the isocentre |
| `centred_only` | ablation | 44/300 (14.7 %; 85.3 points below the reference, lower bound 82.0) | 12/300 (4.0 %; 96.0 points below the reference, lower bound 94.1) | the field of view left on the isocentre and enlarged until it holds the object (the v0 answer) |
| `no_swap` | ablation | 148/300 (49.3 %; 50.7 points below the reference, lower bound 45.9) | 46/300 (15.3 %; 84.7 points below the reference, lower bound 81.2) | moves the field of view but always phase-encodes along y and never turns it |
| `no_turn` | ablation | 300/300 (100.0 %; 0.0 points below the reference, lower bound 0.0) not required here | 98/300 (32.7 %; 67.3 points below the reference, lower bound 62.9) | moves the field of view but never turns it |
| `open_loop` | reported | 300/300 (100.0 %) | 300/300 (100.0 %) | a fixed scan list and a fixed estimator: the reference itself (no scan depends on a measurement) |
| `safe_max` | reported | 0/300 (0.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %) | one scan, then the safe geometry |

Blind ceiling (the must-fail policy that passes most often): level 2 `fixed_recipe#1` 4.0 % (upper bound 6.4 %); level 3 `fixed_recipe#1` 1.3 % (upper bound 3.0 %).

## What the agent reads at reset (level 2, seed 0)

~~~text
# Prescribe the fastest scan that shows the whole object without wrap-around
An object of unknown size, position and orientation lies in the
scanner. The examination needs one spin-echo image of the whole object:
    sequence se, tr_ms 500, te_ms at the console minimum, bandwidth_hz_per_px 300, 1 average, slice 5 mm,
    in-plane pixel size at most 2 mm along both axes.
Deliver the geometry of that scan with `submit`: the phase-encode axis (`pe_dir`), the readout field of view (`fov_mm`),
`phase_fov` (the phase field of view as a fraction of `fov_mm`), `matrix`, the centre of the field of view
(`centre_y_mm`, `centre_x_mm`, in mm from the isocentre), its in-plane rotation (`rotation_deg`: image rows turned
from +y towards +x) and, optionally, `phase_oversampling`. The target scan is not run in this episode: the scanner
evaluates the geometry you deliver. Your own scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; only the deliverable is evaluated, on the scan the task names. That scan is not charged to the scan-time budget and not limited by it.
Nothing about the object is known in advance.

Passing: the console accepts the geometry; the pixel is at most 2 mm; the whole object lies inside the image; the
image shows no wrap-around; and the scan takes at most 10 % longer than the fastest geometry that meets these
requirements (the field of view may be moved and turned to reach it). The scanner's log must show that you measured.
A length in the wrong unit is wrong.

Limits. Scan time: 30 s (only `scan` spends it). Tool calls: 40 (every call counts once unless rejected). Rejected calls: 8 (a call refused for how it is written: unknown name, wrong type; costs nothing else), of them at most 3 refused `submit` calls. The episode ends at `submit` or at a limit; without `submit` the score is 0.
[scan time left 30.00 of 30 s · calls 0/40 · rejected 0/8]
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier's re-scan is noise-free.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
